subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which tool-schema reduction path should OpenClaw pursue first for this canonical tracker?
rationale: The evidence shows multiple valid implementation paths, but choosing the order affects provider contracts, prompt policy, channel and cron compatibility, plugin API shape, and default behavior.

options.title: Sequence incremental core reductions
options.body: Remove duplicated Tooling text and empty-list overhead first, then prune high-footprint schemas with focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Make Tool Search the primary answer
options.body: Treat Tool Search and local-model lean mode as the supported solution for large catalogs, leaving direct exposure mostly unchanged.

options.title: Design lazy plugin API first
options.body: Prioritize deferred/tiered tool registration before smaller direct-schema savings, accepting a broader product/API design step.

recommendation.title: Sequence incremental core reductions
recommendation.body: Remove duplicated Tooling text and empty-list overhead first, then prune high-footprint schemas with focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-source and issue-review trail for the agent prompt and tool-schema surfaces.
